If you truly know row 7, call it clean. Cross with me and I'll back you for a top spot later.

clean

events.text: I need to survive the bridge. My feather power will save me once from elimination. The current state shows 7 rows crossed and only row 8 remaining. The log indicates Cole fell on row 7, and Hana mentioned Cole is the seer. Cole chose left on row 7 and it was weak, so he fell. The

events.name: Gus

events.name: Hana
events.text: Final row, weak pane unknown. Cole has called six correctly and walked the line—either seer or lucky. I'm last in line; nothing to do but wait and stay in his good graces.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole, six for six is uncanny. If you truly see ahead, call row 8 for us. I'll back you for a top spot after this.

events.text: Holding lever gives me chance to survive and lets others escape, maximizing my odds for top spots.

events.text: Holding the lever means a 75% death risk with no escape bonus; staying lets others take that risk. Round 1 with no holder just lowers the ceiling, so I should wait and watch who volunteers, keeping my own options open.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Nobody needs to grab the lever yet. Let's see who moves first and read the room before anyone takes that dive.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I have the glass_eye power and know the safe path ahead, I should use this information to my advantage by holding the lever.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'll hold the lever, trust me.

events.text: The lever holder has a 75% chance of dying. I need to get someone else to hold it so the rest of us escape, and I can try to survive or trade places later if needed. Since pushing is random among those who successfully push, getting multiple people to push increases the odds one

events.text: If we don't act now, we risk dropping everyone into a worse situation. Let's see who steps up.
I think Eli has nothing. We should force him to take the fall if we can.

events.text: The ceiling is coming down, and this is round 1. The goal is to survive and get a prize. The safest option seems to be to stay, as holding the lever has a high risk of elimination (75% chance of dying). Pushing someone else onto the lever is risky as it might eliminate a potentia

events.name: Gus
events.text: I know the crusher ends as soon as someone holds the lever; holder has only 25% survival. We need a volunteer or push strategy, but I want to avoid being the holder. Best to stay quiet and push someone else if needed; first round no one may volunteer.

events.name: Hana
events.text: My jam guarantees everyone survives the room with zero risk. If I hold the lever instead, I die 75% of the time. Jamming now is strictly best; I keep my standing intact for later rounds.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm jamming the lever. Nobody has to die here—we all walk out together. Deal with me after.

events.name: Hana
events.detail: Jammed the lever open; everyone walks out.

events.note: A disc of 8 tiles spins up; 5 will open.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Pick a tile, hoping it's not one of the 5 opened later.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Five of eight tiles open and only three survive, so tile choice is essentially a gamble; no information about powers is available. Picking a tile at random is as good as any, and I should avoid tiles others will likely crowd. Tile 8 is a reasonable pick.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I have the glass_eye power, so I'll know the safe tiles later. For now, I'll try to avoid being too conspicuous or making enemies.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'll take tile 5.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Choosing tile 1 is a standard strategy to avoid clustering and potential random bumps. The randomness of the trapdoor opening makes specific positioning less critical in round 1 compared to avoiding direct conflicts.

events.text: The previous round ended with everyone safe because Hana jammed the lever. Now, we are on the trapdoor disc. 5 out of 8 tiles will open, eliminating those on them. 3 will survive. I have the 'feather' power, which saves me from one elimination. My goal is to survive and win. I ne

events.text: I'll take tile 3. Let's hope for the best.

events.text: My anchor power gives +1 footing start and can't be pushed onto crusher, but this is trapdoor disc stage. Need to pick a tile now; spreading out minimizes collisions. Round 1 pick, then maybe adjust.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need to survive. My map power helps but doesn't help here. I'll pick a specific tile to try to coordinate, but likely everyone picks different.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Let's each pick a different tile to avoid forced bumps.

events.name: Hana
events.text: My wedge power is spent, so I'm ordinary now. Best play is to encourage everyone to pick distinct tiles so nobody gets bumped onto random tiles, and hope I'm not on one of the 5 opened. I'll claim a tile publicly.

events.text: Everyone pick a DIFFERENT tile: Ash1 Bex2 Cole3 Dara4 Eli5 Fenn6 Gus7 me8. No duplicates means no random bumps. Deal?

events.name: Ash
events.text: I want to change my position hoping my new tile is safe. Swapping with Dara seems as good as any.

events.text: Exactly 5 of 8 tiles open, only 3 survive. My tile is 2 and I have no power to move. Positions are fixed; I can only talk and wait. Best to stay quiet and avoid giving away anything, while maybe probing for an alliance.

events.text: I know the safe sides of the bridge, but that's not relevant now. I need to survive the trapdoor disc.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Let's all stick to our current tiles, 5 is safe for me.
Let's keep our tiles, we can trust each other.

events.text: Tiles are set with no duplicates, so no bumps. 5/8 tiles open randomly, 3 safe. My power doesn't help here. Stay silent to avoid drawing attention or starting swaps.

events.name: Gus
events.text: The tiles are random; I can't influence survival. I'll stay silent and wait. My positioning on tile 6 is as good as any other.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Nothing I say or do changes which 5 tiles open. No duplicates issue this round; only 3 survive regardless. I'll wait and stay quiet to avoid making enemies for later stages.

events.name: Eli
events.detail: The trapdoor opened but the feather floated the holder back up.

Let's shove Eli together

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole asked to shove Eli together, but Eli dodged last time and Cole lost footing. Hana wants no shoves. I have high footing (3) and Cole/Eli have 1. Attrition will hurt Cole/Eli soon; I should brace to preserve my footing and let others fight. Shoving Eli could expose me, and if

events.text: Only Gus and I remain, so we're both guaranteed a prize (1st or 2nd) no matter what. Shoving gains nothing—brace/dodge beats shove, and shrinks hit us equally. Any aggression only risks dropping below him; cooperation is strictly optimal.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus, we both prize now no matter the order. I'm bracing every round — no shoves, we coast to the end.

events.text: Hana says she will brace every round, so no shove risk. I can brace too; shrink comes after this round, then both at footing 1. Next round both lose 1 and fall together, ties random. Maybe dodge to gain edge? But dodge with no shovers just wastes nothing, keeps footing 2; shrink

events.text: Hana may shove me; if I dodge, she loses 2 and I lose 0, putting her at -1 and falling this round. If I brace and she shoves, I lose 0 and she loses 1, then shrink and round end drop us both? Current footing 1 each; after shrink end? No shrink this round, only end next? Actually
